body.statement: Fix \(c>0\) and \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\). Under \(P\in\operatorname{ri}(C_c^v)\), the projected empirical law \(\widetilde P_n\) is eventually attainable almost surely and \(L_c^v(\widetilde P_n)\to L_c^v(P)\) and \(U_c^v(\widetilde P_n)\to U_c^v(P)\) almost surely.
body.justification: This is the strongest pointwise plug-in consistency warranted by convex value-function continuity without boundary regularity.
body.gap: The nearest Stieltjes-set estimator uses broader regularity conditions for a different conditional model; it does not verify continuity for the reconstructed feedback cone.
body.consumer: It justifies fixed-slope endpoint estimation for attainable interior empirical designs while displaying the exact boundary excluded from the claim.
body.proof_tex:
First, \(C_c^v\) is convex.  For the weak class this follows by mixing the
eight response-measure families representing two attainable laws.  For the
strict class, if \(\nu_s^j\sim\mu^j\) for \(j=0,1\), then, for
\(0<\lambda<1\),
\[
 \lambda\nu_s^0+(1-\lambda)\nu_s^1
 \sim \lambda\mu^0+(1-\lambda)\mu^1
\]
for every type \(s\); hence strict positivity is preserved.  The same mixture
maps the two observed laws and their APEs to their convex combinations.

Let \(P_0,P_1\in C_c^v\).  Mixing feasible points whose effects are within
\(\epsilon\) of their lower endpoints, and then sending
\(\epsilon\downarrow0\), yields
\[
 L_c^v(\lambda P_0+(1-\lambda)P_1)
 \le \lambda L_c^v(P_0)+(1-\lambda)L_c^v(P_1).
\]
Thus \(L_c^v\) is convex on \(C_c^v\); the same argument with suprema shows
that \(U_c^v\) is concave.  Both are finite by the uniform scalar-effect bound
proved in \(\mathrm{thm{:}fixed\text{-}slope\text{-}endpoints}\).  Applying
\(\mathrm{lem{:}relative\text{-}interior\text{-}convex\text{-}continuity}\)
to \(L_c^v\) and to \(-U_c^v\) proves their continuity at every point of
\(\operatorname{ri}(C_c^v)\), relative to \(\operatorname{aff}(C_c^v)\).

It remains to verify convergence of the argument.  For each of the sixteen
cells let \(Z_i\) be its indicator and \(p\) its probability.  Independence
in \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}units}\), centering, and \(|Z_i-p|\le1\) give
\[
 \mathbb E\left[\left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_i-p)\right)^4\right]
 =\frac{n\mathbb E[(Z_1-p)^4]+3n(n-1)\mathbb E[(Z_1-p)^2]^2}{n^4}
 \le\frac4{n^2}.
\]
Markov's inequality and the union bound therefore imply that, for every
\(\epsilon>0\), the sum over \(n\) of the probabilities of deviations larger
than \(\epsilon\) is finite.  Indeed, the probability of their limsup is at
most the limit, as \(N\to\infty\), of the corresponding tail sum, which is
zero.  Applying this to the countable sequence \(\epsilon=1/k\) and to all
sixteen cells proves \(\widehat P_n\to P\) almost surely.

Orthogonal projection onto an affine subspace is nonexpansive and fixes
\(P\), so \(\widetilde P_n\to P\) almost surely.  The relative-interior
assumption gives \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
 \{Q\in\operatorname{aff}(C_c^v):\|Q-P\|_2<\delta\}\subset C_c^v.
\]
Hence \(\widetilde P_n\) is eventually attainable almost surely.  Relative
continuity of the two value functions now gives the two asserted almost-sure
limits.  No step supplies continuity at a relative-boundary law or permits
\(c\) to vary with \(n\).
